1618.subject: Physics
1618.text: Assertion : A planar circular loop of area $A$ and carrying current $I$ is equivalent to magnetic dipole of dipole moment $M=I A$.Reason : At large distances, magnetic field of circular loop and magnetic dipole is same.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1618.sol:
Magnetic field due to a circular loop 
carrying current I is given as
$B=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 \pi I r^2}{\left(r^2+x^2\right)^{3 / 2}}$
where, $r=$ radius of loop $x=$ distance from centre of loop For large distances, $(x>>r)$,
$\therefore \quad B=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 I A}{x^3}=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 M}{x^3}$
where $M=I A=$ magnetic dipole moment of current loop which is equal to the magnetic field due to magnetic dipole.
Thus, the current loop can be considered as a magnetic dipole.

3415.text:
The correct order about the number of unpaired electrons present in the following complexes is

$\left.\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_$6\right]^{4-} \underset{$\text{ II }}{\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2}  \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}} \underset{\text{ III }}{ \mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{H}$_{{2}} $\mathrm{O}\right)_$6}\right]^{2+}
3415.sol:
I. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6 \mathrm{I}^{4-}\right.$
Atomic number of $\mathrm{Fe}=26$
Ground state configuration of $\mathrm{Fe}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^6 4 s^2\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]$3 d⁶

Since, cyanide is a powerful ligand, therefore, all the electrons will be paired.
Number of unpaired electrons in $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}=0$
II. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$
Atomic number of $\mathrm{Fe}=26$
Ground state configuration of $\mathrm{Fe}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^6 4 s^2\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]$3 d⁶

Number of unpaired electrons in $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}=4$
III. $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$
Atomic number of $\mathrm{Co}=27$
Ground state configuration of $\mathrm{Fe}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 d^7 4 s^2\mathrm{Co}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]$3 d⁷

Number of unpaired electrons in $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}=3$
So, the correct order is II  >  III  >  I.

5839.subject: Chemistry
5839.text: Which one of the following statements is correct for adsorption of solutes on solids in solutions?
options: The extent of adsorption increases with an increase in temperature
The extent of adsorption decreases with an increase of surface area of the adsorbate
The extent of adsorption decreases with an increase in temperature
The extent of adsorption does not depend on the amount of the solute in solution
5839.sol:
(a) The extent of adsorption increases with an increase in temperature is an incorrect statement because an increase in temperature reduces the interaction between the absorbate molecules and adsorbent molecules.
(b) The extent of adsorption decreases with an increase of surface area of the adsorbate is also an incorrect statement as adsorption $\propto$ surface area of adsorbate.
(c) The extent of adsorption decreases with an increased in temperature. \because $\text{ Adsorption } \propto \frac{1}{\text{ temperature }}$ Thus, is the correct statement.
(d) The extent of adsorption does not depend on amount of solute in solution.
This is also an incorrect statement because : $\frac{x}{m} \propto \operatorname{conc} .($ C)^{1 / n} where, $\frac{x}{m}=$ amount of adsorbent $(x)$, adsorbed on given mass $(m)$ of adsorbate and $n=$ an integer. Thus, plot of $\log \frac{x}{m} v s \log C$ gives a straight line upward slope. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

10409.text:
Choose the correct option regarding the following statements
1. \(C_0+C_2+C_4+\ldots+C_n=2^{n-1}\), if \(n\) is even
2. \(C_1+C_3+C_5+\ldots+C_{n-1}=2^{n-1}\), if \(n\) is even
10409.sol:
Since,
\((1+x)^n=C_0+C_1 x+C_2 x²+C_3 x³+\ldots \ldots+C_n x^n\)
On putting \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\) respectively, we get
$\begin{aligned}2^n & =C_0+C_1+C_2+C_3+\ldots \ldots+C_n \\
0 & =C_0-C_1+C_2-C_3+\ldots \ldots+(-1)^n C_n
\end{aligned} and $\(0=C_0-C_1+C_2-C_3+\ldots \ldots+(-1)^n C_n\)
If \(n\) is even , then
\(C_0+C_1+C_2+C_3+\ldots \ldots+C_n=2^n\)...(i)$\text{and })$ C_0-C_1+C_2-C_3+\ldots \ldots+C_n=0\)...(ii)
By adding and subtracting Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
\(C_0+C_2+C_4+\ldots \ldots+C_n=2^{n-1}\)
and \(\quad C_1+C_3+C_5+\ldots \ldots+C_{n-1}=2^{n-1}\)

10592.subject: Mathematics
10592.text: $S$ is the sample space and $A, B$ are two events of a random experiment. Match the items of List A with the items of List B.
10592.sol:
I. A, B are mutually exclusive events
$\Rightarrow P(A \cap B)=0 \quad \therefore \quad P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$
II. A, B are independent events
$\Rightarrow P(A \cap B)=P(A) \cdot P(B)P\left(\frac{\bar{A}}{B}\right)=\frac{P(\bar{A} \cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{P(\bar{A}) \cdot P(B)}{P(B)}=P(\bar{A})=1-P(A)$
III. $A \cap B=A \Rightarrow A \subset B \Rightarrow P(A) \leq P(B)$
IV. $A \cup B=S\Rightarrow P(A \cup B)=1 \Rightarrow P(A)+P(B)-P(A \cap B)=1\Rightarrow P(A)-1+P(B)=P(A \cap B)\Rightarrow P(B)-P(\bar{A})=P(A \cap B)$

12461.text: Angle made by the position vector of the point $( 5, - 4, - 3 )$ with the positive direction of $X -$axis is
12461.sol:
The position vector of the point& $\left(5, - 4, - 3\right)$ is~$5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

We know that~$\overset{^}{i}$~is the unit vector along& $x -$axis

So, the angle between the vector~$5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$~and& $x -$axis will be same as the angle between the vector~$5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$ and~$\overset{^}{i}$.

Let the angle be~$\theta$

$⇒ \left(5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{^}{i} = \left|5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right|\left|\overset{^}{i}\right|cos\theta$

$⇒ 5 = 5\sqrt{2}cos\theta$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{π}{4}$

13338.text: Let \(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}\) and \(\mathbf{w}\) be three vectors in \(R³\). Then, any vector \(Z \in \mathbf{R}^3\) can be written as \(z=a \mathbf{u}+b \mathbf{v}+c \mathbf{w}\) for some scalars \(a, b\) and \(c\) if and only if
options: Each pair of \(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}\) and \(\mathbf{w}\) are not parallel
Each of \(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}\) and \(\mathbf{w}\) can be written as a linear combination of the other two
All have different magnitude and directions
None of the options are correct
13338.sol:
As given vector \(u, v\) and \(\mathbf{w}\) given may be not parallel but they may be antiparallel
So, \(\mathbf{z} \neq a \mathbf{u}+b \mathbf{v}+c \mathbf{w}\)
So first is incorrect.
Also, if \(\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{v}+\mathbf{w}\)
\(\begin{gathered}
\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{w} \\
\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}
\end{gathered}\)
Then, \(\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}+\mathbf{w}=2(\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}+\mathbf{w})\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad \mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}+\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{0} \neq \mathbf{z}\)
So, option (b) is incorrect.
Similarly, option (c) is incorrect.

$\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{{sin}^{3}\theta}{2sin2\theta}$

$3sin2\theta - 2{sin}^{2}\theta$

$tan\theta = 3$

From the geometry of the triangle,

From the equation $\left(1\right)$

$\dfrac{{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}\theta}{2g} = 3$

${u}^{2}{sin}^{2}\theta = 3 \times 2g$

20321.subject: Chemistry
20321.text: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ reactions.
20321.sol:
The rate of an $S_{N}1$ reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation intermediate formed after the departure of the leaving group (bromide ion). The more stable the carbocation, the faster the $S_{N}1$ reaction.

The carbocations formed from the given compounds are:
(I) Benzyl carbocation: $C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with one phenyl ring.
(II) Diphenylmethyl carbocation: $(C_{6}H_{5})_{2}CH^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with two phenyl rings.
(III) 1-Phenylethyl carbocation: $C_{6}H_{5}CH(CH_{3})^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with one phenyl ring and the inductive effect of the methyl group.
(IV) 1,1-Diphenylethyl carbocation: $(C_{6}H_{5})_{2}C(CH_{3})^{+}$, which is stabilized by resonance with two phenyl rings and the inductive effect of the methyl group.

Comparing the stabilities:
1. Compound (I) forms a primary benzylic carbocation (least stable among the options).
2. Compound (III) forms a secondary benzylic carbocation, which is more stable than (I) due to the electron-donating methyl group.
3. Compound (II) forms a secondary carbocation stabilized by two phenyl rings, which is more stable than (III).
4. Compound (IV) forms a tertiary carbocation stabilized by two phenyl rings and one methyl group, making it the most stable.

The order of stability of carbocations is (I) < (III) < (II) < (IV).

Therefore, the increasing order of reactivity towards $S_{N}1$ reactions is (I) < (III) < (II) < (IV).

Answer: I < III < II < IV

21830.subject: Mathematics
21830.text: If ${ }^{35} \mathrm{C}_{x+7}={ }^{35} \mathrm{C}_{4 x-2}$, then the values of $x$ are either
21830.sol:
The property of combinations states that if ^{n}C_{a} = ^{n}C_{b}$, then either $a = b$ or $a + b = n$.

Given ^{35}C_{x+7} = ^{35}C_{4x-2}$, we have two cases.

Case 1: $x + 7 = 4x - 2$.
Rearranging the terms gives $3x = 9$, which implies $x = 3$.

Case 2: $(x + 7) + (4x - 2) = 35$.
Simplifying the expression gives $5x + 5 = 35$.
Subtracting 5 from both sides gives $5x = 30$, which implies $x = 6$.

Thus, the possible values for $x$ are 3 or 6.

Answer: 3 or 6

22247.subject: Mathematics
22247.sol:
Let $x = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$. The expression is $(\cos x - \sin x)(\tan x + \cot x)$.

We know that $\tan x + \cot x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \dfrac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \dfrac{1}{\sin x \cos x}$.

Multiplying by $2$ in the numerator and denominator, we get $\dfrac{2}{2 \sin x \cos x} = \dfrac{2}{\sin 2x}$.

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$, $2x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$. Thus, $\tan x + \cot x = \dfrac{2}{\sin(\pi/6)} = \dfrac{2}{1/2} = 4$.

Now consider the first term: $\cos x - \sin x$.

Using the identity $\cos x - \sin x = \sqrt{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos x - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin x \right) = \sqrt{2} \cos(x + \pi/4)$.

For $x = \pi/12$, $x + \pi/4 = \pi/12 + 3\pi/12 = 4\pi/12 = \pi/3$.

So, $\cos(\pi/12) - \sin(\pi/12) = \sqrt{2} \cos(\pi/3) = \sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

The product is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times 4 = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}$.

Answer: $2 \sqrt{2}$

22447.subject: Physics
22447.text: Which of the following series spectrum of hydrogen atom lies in ultraviolet region?
22447.sol:
The wavelength $\lambda$ of the spectral lines in the hydrogen atom is given by the Rydberg formula: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right), where $ n_1$ is the lower energy level and $n_2$ is the higher energy level.

For the Lyman series, $n_1 = 1$ and $n_2 = 2, 3, 4, \dots$. The transitions to the ground state ($n_1 = 1$) involve large energy differences, which correspond to the ultraviolet region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

For the Balmer series, $n_1 = 2$, which lies in the visible region.

For the Paschen series, $n_1 = 3$, which lies in the infrared region.

For the Brackett series, $n_1 = 4$, which lies in the infrared region.

For the Pfund series, $n_1 = 5$, which lies in the infrared region.

Therefore, the Lyman series is the only one among the given options that lies in the ultraviolet region.

Answer: Lyman series$

22792.sol:
The torque experienced by an electric dipole in a uniform electric field is given by:

$\tau = pE \sin\theta$

Substituting the given values:

$8\sqrt{3} = pE \sin 60^{}^{\circ}$

$8\sqrt{3} = pE \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)

$pE = 16$

The potential energy of the dipole in the electric field is given by:

$U = -pE \cos$\theta

$U = -16 \cos 60^{}^{\circ}$

$U = -16 $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$U = -8 \text{ J}$

Answer: $-8J$

22839.subject: Physics
22839.text: Two charges '$-q$' each are fixed, separated by distance '$2 d$'. A third charge '$q$' of mass '$m$' placed at the mid-point is displaced slightly by '$x$' $(x< < d)$ perpendicular to the line joining the two fixed charges as shown in Fig. The time period of oscillation of '$q$' will be
22839.sol:
Let the two fixed charges $-q$ be located at $(-d, 0)$ and $(d, 0)$. The charge $q$ is at $(0, x)$. The distance $r$ between the charge $q$ and each of the fixed charges is $r = \sqrt{d^2 + x^2}$.

The force exerted by each fixed charge on $q$ is $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q^2}{r^2}$. The vertical component of the force from each charge is $F_y = F \cos \theta$, where $\cos \theta = \dfrac{x}{r}$.

The net restoring force on $q$ is $F_{net} = -2 F_y = -2 \left( \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q^2}{r^2} \right) \left( \dfrac{x}{r} \right) = -\dfrac{q^2 x}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}$.

Since $x \ll d$, $r = \sqrt{d^2 + x^2} \approx d$. Thus, $F_{net} \approx -\dfrac{q^2 x}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 d^3}$.

The equation of motion is $m \dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -\left( \dfrac{q^2}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 d^3} \right) x$. This represents simple harmonic motion with angular frequency $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{q^2}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 m d^3}}$.

The time period $T$ is given by $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{2\pi\varepsilon_0 m d^3}{q^2}} = \sqrt{4\pi^2 \dfrac{2\pi\varepsilon_0 m d^3}{q^2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8\pi^3 \varepsilon_0 m d^3}{q^2}}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{T}=\sqrt{\dfrac{8 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{ m} \pi^3 \mathrm{ d}^3}{\mathrm{q}^2}}$

27278.subject: Chemistry
27278.sol:
Benzenesulphonyl chloride $\left({C}_{6}{H}_{5}{SO}_{2}Cl\right)$, which is also known as Hinsberg's reagent, reacts with primary and secondary amines to form sulphonamides.

The Hinsberg test is based on the production of sulfonamides. An amine interacts with benzene sulfonyl chloride in the Hinsberg test. Due to the inability of tertiary amines to form stable sulfonamides, any product produced is either a primary or secondary amine. If the resulting sulfonamide dissolves in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution, it is a primary amine. It is a secondary amine if the sulfonamide is insoluble in aqueous sodium hydroxide and hydrogen chloride.

32495.subject: Chemistry
32495.text: Which of the following statements about colloids is false?
options:
When silver nitrate solution is added to potassium iodide solution, a negatively charged colloidal solution is formed

Freezing point of colloidal solution is lower than true solution at same concentration of a solute

Colloidal particles can pass through ordinary filter paper

When excess of electrolyte is added to colloidal solution, colloidal particle will be precipitated
32495.sol:
(a) Colloidal particles are so small that they can pass through ordinary filter paper. Also, they cannot be seen with ordinary microscope.
(b) Freezing point of colloidal solution is same as that of true solution at same concentration of a solute. The depression in freezing point is a colloidal property and depends on the number of solute particles and independent of size or shape of solute particles.
(c) When silver nitrate solution is added to potassium iodide solution, a negatively charged colloidal solution is formed due to selective adsorption of $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ion from the dispersion medium. However, if the order of addition is reversed, i.e, potassium iodide solution is added to silver nitrate solution, due to selective adsorption of $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$ion from the dispersion medium, a positively charged colloidal solution is obtained.
(d) When excess of electrolyte is added to colloidal solution, colloidal particle will be precipitated. Although electrolytes in minute quantities are necessary for the stability of colloids, they cause coagulation of disperse phase if present in large quantities.

32856.text: If the tangent to the curve $y = {x}^{3} - {x}^{2} + x$ at the point $\left(a, b\right)$ is also tangent to the curve $y = 5{x}^{2} + 2x - 25$ at the point $\left(2, - 1\right)$, then $\left|2a + 9b\right|$ is equal to ______.
32856.sol:
Given,

Curve $y = 5{x}^{2} + 2x - 25$

Now differentiating to find slope at point $P\left(2, - 1\right) we get,

${y}^{'} = 10x + 2 ⇒ {y}_{P}^{'} = 22$

Now tangent to curve at $P$ will be,

$y + 1 = 22$\left(x - 2\right)$

$⇒ y = 22x - 45$

Now the tangent is also tangent to the curve $y = {x}^{3} - {x}^{2} + x$ and passing through $\left(a, b\right)$ so plottnig the diagram we get,

Now differentiating the curve $y = {x}^{3} - {x}^{2} + x$ we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3{x}^{2} - 2x + 1$

${\dfrac{dy}{dx}}_{Q = \left(a, b\right)} = 3{a}^{2} - 2a + 1$

So, equating with tangent slope we get,

$3{a}^{2} - 2a + 1 = 22$

$⇒ 3{a}^{2} - 2a - 21 = 0$

$⇒ 3{a}^{2} - 9a + 7a - 21 = 0$

$⇒ \left(3a + 7\right)\left(a - 3\right) = 0$

Now from curve $b = {a}^{3} - {a}^{2} + a$

So, at $a = 3 ⇒ b = 21$

Also $a = 3 \text{$ and } b = 21 are satisfying the line $y = 22x - 45$

So, $\left|2a + 9b\right| = \left|2 \times 3 + 9 \times 21\right| = 195$

Note at $a = - 7 / 3$ tangent will be parallel so it is rejected

33275.subject: Mathematics
33275.text: If the coefficients of the middle terms in the binomial expansions of $(1 + \alpha x)^{26}$ and $(1 - \alpha x)^{28}$, $\alpha \neq 0$, are equal, then the value of $\alpha$ is:
33275.sol:
The expansion of $(1 + \alpha x)^{26}$ has $27$ terms. The middle term is $T_{14}$.

The coefficient of the middle term is $^{26}C_{13} \alpha^{13}$.

The expansion of $(1 - \alpha x)^{28}$ has $29$ terms. The middle term is $T_{15}$.

The coefficient of the middle term is $^{28}C_{14} (-\alpha)^{14} = ^{28}C_{14} \alpha^{14}$.

Equating the two coefficients:

$^{26}C_{13} \alpha^{13} = ^{28}C_{14} \alpha^{14}$

Since $\alpha \neq 0$, dividing by $\alpha^{13}$ gives:

$\alpha = \dfrac{^{26}C_{13}}{^{28}C_{14}}$

Expanding the combinations using factorials:

$^{28}C_{14} = \dfrac{28!}{14! 14!} = \dfrac{28 \times 27 \times 26!}{14 \times 13! \times 14 \times 13!} = \dfrac{28 \times 27}{14 \times 14} \times \dfrac{26!}{13! 13!}$

$^{28}C_{14} = \dfrac{27}{7} \times ^{26}C_{13}$

Substituting this back:

$\alpha = \dfrac{^{26}C_{13}}{\dfrac{27}{7} \times ^{26}C_{13}} = \dfrac{7}{27}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7}{27}$

35473.text: Let $f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{16x + 24}{x^2 + 2x - 15}\right) dx$. If $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$ and $f(7) = \log_e(2^{\alpha} \cdot 3^{\beta})$, $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to:
35473.sol:
The given integral is $f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{16x + 24}{x^2 + 2x - 15}\right) dx$.

Factorizing the denominator, we get $x^2 + 2x - 15 = (x + 5)(x - 3)$.

Using partial fractions, we can write:

$\dfrac{16x + 24}{(x + 5)(x - 3)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 5} + \dfrac{B}{x - 3}$

$16x + 24 = A(x - 3) + B(x + 5)$

Substituting $x = 3$, we get $72 = 8B \Rightarrow B = 9$.

Substituting $x = -5$, we get $-56 = -8A \Rightarrow A = 7$.

Therefore, the integral becomes:

$f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{7}{x + 5} + \dfrac{9}{x - 3}\right) dx$

$f(x) = 7 \log_e|x + 5| + 9 \log_e|x - 3| + C$

Given $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$, we substitute $x = 4$:

$f(4) = 7 \log_e(9) + 9 \log_e(1) + C = 14 \log_e(3) + C$

Since $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$, we get $C = 0$.

Thus, $f(x) = 7 \log_e|x + 5| + 9 \log_e|x - 3|$.

Now, substituting $x = 7$:

$f(7) = 7 \log_e(12) + 9 \log_e(4)$

$f(7) = 7 \log_e(2^2 \cdot 3) + 9 \log_e(2^2)$

$f(7) = 7(2 \log_e(2) + \log_e(3)) + 18 \log_e(2)$

$f(7) = 14 \log_e(2) + 7 \log_e(3) + 18 \log_e(2)$

$f(7) = 32 \log_e(2) + 7 \log_e(3)$

$f(7) = \log_e(2^{32} \cdot 3^7)$

Comparing this with $f(7) = \log_e(2^{\alpha} \cdot 3^{\beta})$, we get $\alpha = 32$ and $\beta = 7$.

Therefore, $\alpha + \beta = 32 + 7 = 39$.

Answer: $39$

35962.text: Consider the matrices $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$. If matrices P and Q are such that $PA = B$ and $AQ = B$, then the absolute value of the sum of the diagonal elements of $2(P + Q)$ is _______.
35962.sol:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$, we find its determinant:

$|A| = (2)(-2) - (-2)(4) = 4$

Since $|A| \neq 0$, $A$ is invertible. The inverse of $A$ is:

$A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 \\ -4 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1/2 & 1/2 \\ -1 & 1/2 \end{bmatrix}$

We are given $PA = B \Rightarrow P = BA^{-1}$ and $AQ = B \Rightarrow Q = A^{-1}B$.

Using the cyclic property of trace $\text{Tr}(XY) = \text{Tr}(YX)$, we have:

$\text{Tr}(P) = \text{Tr}(BA^{-1}) = \text{Tr}(A^{-1}B) = \text{Tr}(Q)$

Let us calculate $\text{Tr}(P)$ by finding the diagonal elements of $P = BA^{-1}$:

$P = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} -1/2 & 1/2 \\ -1 & 1/2 \end{bmatrix}$

The diagonal elements of $P$ are:

$P_{11} = 3\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 9(-1) = -\dfrac{21}{2}$

$P_{22} = 1\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 3\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2$

$\text{Tr}(P) = P_{11} + P_{22} = -\dfrac{21}{2} + 2 = -\dfrac{17}{2}$

Since $\text{Tr}(P) = \text{Tr}(Q) = -\dfrac{17}{2}$, the sum of the diagonal elements of $2(P + Q)$ is:

$\text{Tr}(2(P + Q)) = 2(\text{Tr}(P) + \text{Tr}(Q)) = 2\left(-\dfrac{17}{2} - \dfrac{17}{2}\right) = 2(-17) = -34$

The absolute value is $|-34| = 34$.

Answer: $34$

The $x$ intercept of the line $3x + 4y - 24 = 0$ can be obtained by putting $y = 0$ i.e. $3x - 24 = 0$

$⇒ x = 8$

Hence, the point $A$ is $\left(8, 0\right) .$

Now, the $y$ intercept of the line $3x + 4y - 24 = 0$ can be obtained by putting $x = 0$ i.e. $4y - 24 = 0$

$⇒ y = 6$

Hence, the point $B$ is $\left(0, 6\right) .$

In $∆ OAB,$ we have $OA = b = 8, OB = a = 6$ and $AB = c = \sqrt{{\left(8 - 0\right)}^{2} + {\left(0 - 6\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = 10$ units.

And, we know that the co-ordinates of incentre $I$ of a triangle with vertices $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right), \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{3}, {y}_{3}\right)$ and having length of the sides opposite to these vertices as $a, b$ and $c,$ respectively, is

$I ≡ \left(\dfrac{a{x}_{1} + b{x}_{2} + c{x}_{3}}{a + b + c}, \dfrac{a{y}_{1} + b{y}_{2} + c{y}_{3}}{a + b + c}\right)$

$⇒ I ≡ \left(\dfrac{6\left(8\right) + 8\left(0\right) + 10\left(0\right)}{24}, \dfrac{6\left(0\right) + 8\left(6\right) + 10\left(0\right)}{24}\right)$

$⇒ I = \left(2, 2\right) .$

Substituting the given values in equation (i)

$2 = 2 \times {10}^{28} \times 25 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 1 .6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times {v}_{d} ⇒ {v}_{d} = \dfrac{2}{2 \times {10}^{28} \times 25 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 1 .6 \times {10}^{- 19}}$

$⇒ {v}_{d} = \dfrac{1}{25 \times 1 .6 \times 1000}m{s}^{- 1} = 25 \times {10}^{- 6}m{s}^{- 1}$

42798.text: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude A. Its speed is tripled at the instant that it is at a distance $\dfrac{2A}{3}$ from equilibrium position. The new amplitude of the motion is:

New SHM will be,

$5{A}^{2} = {A}_{N}^{2} - \dfrac{4{A}^{2}}{9}$

${A}_{N}^{2} = \dfrac{49{A}^{2}}{9}$

${A}_{N} = \dfrac{7A}{3}$

45407.subject: Chemistry
45407.text: Which of the following undergoes nucleophilic substitution exclusively by $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ mechanism?
45407.sol:
Aliphatic $S_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ reaction is carried out in two steps.
In form of slow step
Step (i) carbonium (carbocation) ion is formed and its formation is based upon the stability Stability order of carbocation
$\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2\gt\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3\gt\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2$
and in step (ii) nucleophile is attracted towards the carbonium ion in form of fast step to give final product.
Hence, in benzyl chloride, ethyl chloride and isopropyl chloride order of $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ reaction is benzyl chloride $\gt$ isopropyl chloride $\gt$ ethyl chloride
In chlorobenzene, mechanism of $S_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ reaction is differ to aliphatic alkyl halide. The aryl halides are much less reactive as compared to alkyl halides, towards nucleophilic reagents in either $S_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ or $S_{\mathrm{N}} 2$ reaction.
The carbon-halogen bond in the aryl halide is quite strong and only forcing conditions can break up this bond.
Hence,
Step (i) $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{ Slow }} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2+\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$
Rate $\propto\left[\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl}\right]$
Step (ii) $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2+\mathrm{Nu}^{-} \xrightarrow{\text{ Fast }} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Nu}$

47282.subject: Biology
47282.text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement-I: Baculoviruses are pathogens that attack nematodes.
Statement-II: Baculoviruses are used as biological control agents in ecologically sensitive areas as they are species-specific in their action.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
47282.sol:
Baculoviruses are pathogens that attack insects and other arthropods, not nematodes. Therefore, Statement-I is false.

The majority of baculoviruses used as biological control agents belong to the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus. These viruses are excellent candidates for species-specific, narrow spectrum insecticidal applications. They have no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish, or even non-target insects. This makes them highly suitable for use in ecologically sensitive areas or in integrated pest management (IPM) programmes. Therefore, Statement-II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true

50174.text: The concentric spheres of radii $R$ and $r$ have positive charges $q_{1}$ and $q_{2}$ with equal surface charge densities. What is the electric potential at their common centre?
50174.sol:
Potential at the centre due to sphere with radius $R$,
$V_{1}=\frac{q_{1}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R}$
Potential at the centre due to sphere with radius $r$,
$V_{2}=\frac{q_{2}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} r}$
Given, surface charge densities for both spheres
$\sigma=\sigma_{R}=\sigma_{r}$
i.e.,
$\begin{aligned}
\text{ i.e., } & \frac{q_{1}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R^{2}} &=\frac{q_{2}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} r^{2}} \\
\Rightarrow & q_{1} &=\frac{R^{2}}{r^{2}} q_{2}
\end{aligned}$
Total potential at the centre due to both spheres
$\begin{aligned}
V &=V_{1}+V_{2} \\
&=\frac{q_{1}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R}+\frac{q_{2}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} r}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}}\left(\frac{q_{1}}{R}+\frac{q_{2}}{r}\right) \\
&=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}}\left(\frac{R^{2}}{r^{2}} \frac{q_{2}}{R}\right)+\frac{q_{2}}{r}=\frac{q_{2}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}}\left(\frac{R+r}{r^{2}}\right) \\
&=\frac{q_{2}}{4 \pi r^{2} \varepsilon_{0}}(R+r)=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}}(R+r)
\end{aligned}$

54846.subject: Chemistry
54846.text: Which of the following alcohols on addition of Lucas reagent reacts fast and turns the reagent turbid instantly.
54846.sol:
Lucas reagent is a mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$.

The reaction of alcohols with Lucas reagent proceeds via an $S_N1$ mechanism, which involves the formation of a carbocation intermediate.

The rate of reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation formed. The order of stability of carbocations is tertiary > secondary > primary. Therefore, the reactivity of alcohols towards Lucas reagent follows the order: tertiary > secondary > primary.

Tertiary alcohols react instantly to form an insoluble alkyl halide, producing immediate turbidity.

Secondary alcohols react in about 5 minutes to produce turbidity.

Primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

Among the given options, tert-butyl alcohol is a tertiary alcohol, so it forms a stable tertiary carbocation and reacts instantly to give turbidity.

n-butyl alcohol and iso-butyl alcohol are primary alcohols, while sec-butyl alcohol is a secondary alcohol.

Answer: tert - Butyl alcohol

56831.subject: Chemistry
56831.text: Which of the following reaction is possible at anode?
56831.sol:
At the anode, oxidation takes place. Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons.

Analyzing the given reactions:

$\text{F}_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2\text{F}^-$ involves the gain of electrons, hence it is a reduction reaction.

$2\text{H}^+ + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}$ involves the gain of electrons, hence it is a reduction reaction.

$\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + 1e^-$ involves the loss of an electron, hence it is an oxidation reaction.

$\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}(s)$ involves the gain of electrons, hence it is a reduction reaction.

Since only the third reaction represents oxidation, it is the only reaction possible at the anode.

Answer: $\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + 1e^-$

The standard enthalpy of formation of water is the enthalpy change of the system for the given reaction.

$\Delta H_{\text{sys}} = -286\ \text{kJ} = -286000\ \text{J}$

The heat absorbed by the surroundings at constant pressure is given by:

$q_{\text{surr}} = -\Delta H_{\text{sys}} = 286000\ \text{J}$

The change in entropy of the surroundings is calculated as:

$\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = \dfrac{q_{\text{surr}}}{T}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = \dfrac{286000}{298} = 959.7\ \text{J K}^{-1}$

Answer: $959.7\ \text{JK}^{-1}$

61674.subject: Mathematics
61674.text: If $x^3 + y^3 = 6$ and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \cdot \dfrac{d^2x}{dy^2} = \dfrac{m}{(xy)^n}$, where $m, n \in R$ then $\dfrac{m}{n} = $
61674.sol:
Given $x^3 + y^3 = 6$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$3x^2 + 3y^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x^2}{y^2}$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x^2}{y^2}\right) = -\dfrac{y^2(2x) - x^2\left(2y \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}{y^4}$

Substituting $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x^2}{y^2}$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\dfrac{2xy^2 - 2x^2y\left(-\dfrac{x^2}{y^2}\right)}{y^4} = -\dfrac{2xy^2 + \dfrac{2x^4}{y}}{y^4} = -\dfrac{2x(y^3 + x^3)}{y^5}$

Since $x^3 + y^3 = 6$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\dfrac{12x}{y^5}$

By symmetry, differentiating $x^3 + y^3 = 6$ with respect to $y$ twice gives:

$\dfrac{d^2x}{dy^2} = -\dfrac{12y}{x^5}$

Multiplying the two second derivatives:

Comparing with $\dfrac{m}{(xy)^n}$, we get $m = 144$ and $n = 4$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{144}{4} = 36$.

Answer: $36$

62973.text: The correct simplified circuit diagram for the logical statement $[\{\mathrm{q} \wedge(\sim \mathrm{q} \vee \mathrm{r})\} \wedge\{\sim \mathrm{p} \vee(\mathrm{p} \wedge \sim \mathrm{r})\}] \vee(\mathrm{p} \wedge \mathrm{r})$ where $\mathrm{p}, \mathrm{q}, \mathrm{r}$ represent switches $\mathrm{s}_1, \mathrm{ s}_2, \mathrm{ s}_3$ respectively.
62973.sol:
The logical expression $[q \wedge ({\sim}q \vee r)] \wedge [{\sim}p \vee (p \wedge {\sim}r)] \vee (p \wedge r)$ simplifies using distributive and identity laws.

Applying the distributive law to $q \wedge ({\sim}q \vee r)$ yields $(q \wedge {\sim}q) \vee (q \wedge r)$, which simplifies to $q \wedge r$ since $q \wedge {\sim}q$ is a contradiction.

Similarly, ${\sim}p \vee (p \wedge {\sim}r)$ distributes to $({\sim}p \vee p) \wedge ({\sim}p \vee {\sim}r)$ and reduces to ${\sim}p \vee {\sim}r$ as ${\sim}p \vee p$ is a tautology.

Substituting, the expression becomes $[(q \wedge r) \wedge ({\sim}p \vee {\sim}r)] \vee (p \wedge r)$. Distributing $(q \wedge r) \wedge ({\sim}p \vee {\sim}r)$ gives $[(q \wedge r) \wedge {\sim}p] \vee [q \wedge (r \wedge {\sim}r)]$, where $r \wedge {\sim}r$ is false, simplifying to $q \wedge r \wedge {\sim}p$.

The expression is now $(q \wedge r \wedge {\sim}p) \vee (p \wedge r)$. Factoring out $r$ results in $r \wedge [({\sim}p \wedge q) \vee p]$, and simplifying $({\sim}p \wedge q) \vee p$ distributes to $({\sim}p \vee p) \wedge (q \vee p)$, yielding $q \vee p$.

The final logical form is $r \wedge (q \vee p)$.

Mapping to switching circuits where $p = s_1$, $q = s_2$, $r = s_3$, $\wedge$ denotes series, and $\vee$ denotes parallel, the expression represents $s_3$ in series with the parallel combination of $s_2$ and $s_1$, corresponding to option B.

$\boxed{B}$

63150.subject: Mathematics
63150.text: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} a & 1 \\ 1 & b \end{bmatrix}$, where $a$ and $b$ are the roots of the equation $x^2 - 4x + 2 = 0$. If $A + A^{-1} = kI_2$, then the value of $k$ is ____
63150.sol:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} a & 1 \\ 1 & b \end{bmatrix}$

Since $a$ and $b$ are roots of $x^2 - 4x + 2 = 0$, we have $a + b = 4$ and $ab = 2$.

The determinant of $A$ is $|A| = ab - 1 = 2 - 1 = 1$.

The inverse of $A$ is $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \begin{bmatrix} b & -1 \\ -1 & a \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} b & -1 \\ -1 & a \end{bmatrix}$.

Now, $A + A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} a & 1 \\ 1 & b \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} b & -1 \\ -1 & a \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} a+b & 0 \\ 0 & a+b \end{bmatrix}$.

Substituting $a + b = 4$, we get $A + A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} = 4I_2$.

Comparing with $A + A^{-1} = kI_2$, we get $k = 4$.

63635.text:
If a random variable $X$ has p.d.f.
$\mathrm{f}(x)= \begin{cases}\frac{a x^2}{2}+\mathrm{b} x & , \text{ if } 1 \leqslant x \leqslant 3 \\ 0 & , \text{ otherwise }\end{cases}$
and $f(2)=2$, then the values of $a$ and $b$ are, respectively
63635.sol:
The probability density function is $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{a x^2}{2} + b x & \text{if } 1 \leq x \leq 3 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$ with conditions $f(2) = 2$ and $\int_1^3 f(x) dx = 1$.

Substituting $x = 2$ yields $\frac{4a}{2} + 2b = 2$, simplifying to $a + b = 1$.

The integral becomes $\int_1^3 \left(\frac{a x^2}{2} + b x\right) dx = \left[\frac{a x^3}{6} + \frac{b x^2}{2}\right]_1^3 = \left(\frac{27a}{6} + \frac{9b}{2}\right) - \left(\frac{a}{6} + \frac{b}{2}\right) = \frac{13a}{3} + 4b = 1$.

Clearing fractions gives $13a + 12b = 3$.

Solving the system $a + b = 1$ and $13a + 12b = 3$, substitute $b = 1 - a$ to obtain $13a + 12(1 - a) = a + 12 = 3$, so $a = -9$ and $b = 10$.

These values correspond to option B.

64389.text: The equation of the plane containing the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{z}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{5} = \dfrac{y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{\lambda}$ is
64389.sol:
For the two lines to be coplanar, the shortest distance between them must be zero.

The first line passes through $A(1, -1, 0)$ with direction ratios $\vec{d}_1 = (2, \lambda, 2)$.

The second line passes through $B(-1, -1, 0)$ with direction ratios $\vec{d}_2 = (5, 2, \lambda)$.

The vector joining the points is $\vec{AB} = (-2, 0, 0)$.

The condition for coplanarity is $[\vec{AB}, \vec{d}_1, \vec{d}_2] = 0$:

\begin{vmatrix} -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & \lambda & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & \lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0$

$-2(\lambda^2 - 4) = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = \pm 2$

Case 1: \lambda = 2$

$\vec{d}_1 = (2, 2, 2)$ and $\vec{d}_2 = (5, 2, 2)$.

The normal vector to the plane is $\vec{n} = \vec{d}_1 \times \vec{d}_2 = (0, 6, -6)$, which is parallel to $(0, 1, -1)$.

The equation of the plane passing through $A(1, -1, 0)$ is:

$0(x - 1) + 1(y + 1) - 1(z - 0) = 0 \Rightarrow y - z + 1 = 0$

Case 2: $\lambda = -2$

$\vec{d}_1 = (2, -2, 2)$ and $\vec{d}_2 = (5, 2, -2)$.

The normal vector to the plane is $\vec{n} = \vec{d}_1 \times \vec{d}_2 = (0, 14, 14)$, which is parallel to $(0, 1, 1)$.

The equation of the plane passing through $A(1, -1, 0)$ is:

$0(x - 1) + 1(y + 1) + 1(z - 0) = 0 \Rightarrow y + z + 1 = 0$

Combining both cases, the equation of the plane is $y \pm z + 1 = 0$.

Answer: $y \pm z + 1 = 0$

64391.subject: Mathematics
64391.text: For the line $\dfrac{x+1}{1} = \dfrac{y-2}{2} = \dfrac{z+3}{3}, identify the incorrect statement among the following.$
options: It can be represented by equation $\dfrac{x+2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z+6}{3}$
It lies in the plane $x - 2y + z + 8 = 0$
It is perpendicular to the plane $x - 2y + z = 0$
64391.sol:
The given line is $\dfrac{x+1}{1} = \dfrac{y-2}{2} = \dfrac{z+3}{3} = \lambda$.

Any point on the line is of the form $(\lambda - 1, 2\lambda + 2, 3\lambda - 3)$.

For $\lambda = -1$, the point is $(-2, 0, -6)$. Since the direction ratios remain the same, the line can be represented as $\dfrac{x+2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z+6}{3}$. Thus, the first statement is correct.

Substituting the general point into the plane $x - 2y + z + 8 = 0$, we get $(\lambda - 1) - 2(2\lambda + 2) + (3\lambda - 3) + 8 = \lambda - 1 - 4\lambda - 4 + 3\lambda - 3 + 8 = 0$, which is true for all $\lambda$. Thus, the line lies in the plane, making the second statement correct.

For $\lambda = 1$, the point is $(0, 4, 0)$. Thus, the line passes through $(0, 4, 0)$, making the fourth statement correct.

The direction ratios of the line are $(1, 2, 3)$ and the normal to the plane $x - 2y + z = 0$ has direction ratios $(1, -2, 1)$. For the line to be perpendicular to the plane, their direction ratios must be proportional. Since $\dfrac{1}{1} \neq \dfrac{2}{-2} \neq \dfrac{3}{1}$, the line is not perpendicular to the plane. Thus, the third statement is incorrect.

Answer: It is perpendicular to the plane $x - 2y + z = 0$

66073.text: A parallel plate capacitor having plate area 'A' and separation 'd' is charged to a potential difference ' $V$ '. The charging battery is disconnected and the plates are pulled apart to four times the initial separation. The work required to increase the distance between the plates is (\epsilon_0=$ permittivity of free space)$
66073.sol:
The initial capacitance is $C_1 = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$, so with potential difference $V$, the stored charge is $Q = C_1V = \frac{\epsilon_0 A V}{d}$ and the initial energy $U_1 = \frac{1}{2} C_1 V^2 = \frac{1}{2} \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d} V^2$.

After disconnecting the battery, charge $Q$ remains constant while plate separation increases to $4d$, giving new capacitance $C_2 = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{4d}$. The final energy is then $U_2 = \frac{Q^2}{2C_2} = \frac{(\epsilon_0 A V/d)^2}{2(\epsilon_0 A/4d)} = \frac{4 \epsilon_0 A V^2}{2d} = \frac{2 \epsilon_0 A V^2}{d}$.

The work done equals the energy change: $W = U_2 - U_1 = \frac{2 \epsilon_0 A V^2}{d} - \frac{1}{2} \frac{\epsilon_0 A V^2}{d} = \frac{3}{2} \frac{\epsilon_0 A V^2}{d}$.

$\boxed{\text{D}}$

66574.text: Photoelectric emission takes place from a certain metal at threshold frequency $v$. If the radiation of frequency $4 v$ is incident on the metal plate, the maximum velocity of the emitted photoelectrons will be ( $\mathrm{m}=$ mass of photoelectron, $\mathrm{h}=$ Planck's constant)
66574.sol:
According to Einstein’s photoelectric equation, $hf = \phi + K_{\text\max}$, where $h$ is Planck’s constant, $f$ is the incident frequency, $\phi$ is the work function, and $K_{\text\max}$ is the maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons.

Given the threshold frequency $v$, the work function is $\phi = hv$.

For incident frequency $4v$, the photoelectric equation becomes $h(4v) = hv + K_{\text\max}$. Solving yields $K_{\text\max} = 3hv$.

Since $K_{\text\max} = \frac{1}{2} m v_{\text\max^2$, equating gives $\frac{1}{2} m v_{\text\max^2 = 3hv$.

Solving for $v_{\text\max}$, we find $v_{\text\max^2 = \frac{6hv}{m}$, so $v_{\text\max} = \sqrt{\frac{6hv}{m}}$, which corresponds to option A.

67227.text: A uniform solid sphere of mass ' m ' and radius ' r ' is surrounded by a uniform thin spherical shell of radius ' $2 r$ ' and mass ' $m$ ' then the gravitational field
options: $at a distance of 15 r from the centre is \frac{2}{9} \frac{\mathrm{Gm}}{\mathrm{r}^2}$
at a distance of $(2 \cdot 5) \mathrm{r}$ from the centre is $\frac{8}{25} \frac{\mathrm{Gm}}{\mathrm{r}^2}$
at a distance of $(1 \cdot 5) \mathrm{r}$ from the centre is zero.
between the sphere and spherical shell is uniform.
67227.sol:
The gravitational field at any point results from superposition of contributions from the solid sphere and spherical shell, each with mass $m$. For a solid sphere of radius $r$: inside ($d < r$), $E = \frac{GMd}{r^3}$; outside ($d \ge r$), $E = \frac{GM}{d^2}$. For a spherical shell of radius $2r$: inside ($d < 2r$), $E = 0$; outside ($d \ge 2r$), $E = \frac{GM}{d^2}$.

At distance $1.5r$ from center, the point lies outside the sphere ($1.5r > r$) and inside the shell ($1.5r < 2r$). Thus $E_{\text{total}} = \frac{Gm}{(1.5r)^2} + 0 = \frac{4}{9} \frac{Gm}{r^2}$, rejecting options A and C.

At distance $2.5r$ from center, the point lies outside both distributions. Hence $E_{\text{total}} = \frac{Gm}{(2.5r)^2} + \frac{Gm}{(2.5r)^2} = \frac{8}{25} \frac{Gm}{r^2}$, confirming option B.

In the region between sphere and shell ($r < d < 2r$), the field varies as $E = \frac{Gm}{d^2}$ due to the sphere alone, which depends on $d$ and is therefore non-uniform, rejecting option D.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

79241.subject: Mathematics
79241.text: A force $\vec{F} = 2\hat{i} - \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ is applied at the point $A(1, 2, 5)$. If its moment about the point $B(-1, -2, 3)$ is $16\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + 2\lambda\hat{k}$, then what is the value of $\lambda$?
79241.sol:
The position vector of the point of application $A$ with respect to point $B$ is $\vec{r} = \vec{r}_A - \vec{r}_B$.

$\vec{r} = (1 - (-1))\hat{i} + (2 - (-2))\hat{j} + (5 - 3)\hat{k} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

The moment of the force about point $B$ is given by $\vec{M} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$.

$\vec{M} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 2 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } 2 \\ 2 \text{ and } -\lambda \text{ and } 5 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{M} = \hat{i}(20 + 2\lambda) - \hat{j}(10 - 4) + \hat{k}(-2\lambda - 8)$

$\vec{M} = (20 + 2\lambda)\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - (2\lambda + 8)\hat{k}$

It is given that $\vec{M} = 16\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + 2\lambda\hat{k}$.

Comparing the coefficients of $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{k}$:

$20 + 2\lambda = 16 \Rightarrow 2\lambda = -4 \Rightarrow \lambda = -2$

$-2\lambda - 8 = 2\lambda \Rightarrow 4\lambda = -8 \Rightarrow \lambda = -2$

Both equations yield $\lambda = -2$.

Answer: $-2$

80993.subject: Chemistry
80993.text: $2\text{A}\xrightarrow{k}\text{B}$ is a zero-order reaction, where $k=1.0$ mol L$^{-1}$ min$^{-1}$. If the initial concentration of A is $2$ M, then the time taken to complete $75\%$ of the reaction will be
80993.sol:
For a zero-order reaction $2\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$, the rate of reaction is expressed as:

$\text{Rate} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\text{A}]}{dt} = k$

$\Rightarrow -\dfrac{d[\text{A}]}{dt} = 2k$

Integrating this equation, we get the integrated rate law:

$[\text{A}]_0 - [\text{A}]_t = 2kt$

Given:
Initial concentration, $[\text{A}]_0 = 2$ M
Rate constant, $k = 1.0$ mol L$^{-1}$ min$^{-1}$

For $75\%$ completion of the reaction, the amount of A reacted is:

$[\text{A}]_0 - [\text{A}]_t = \dfrac{75}{100} \times 2 = 1.5$ M

Substituting these values into the integrated rate equation:

$1.5 = 2 \times 1.0 \times t$

$2t = 1.5$

$t = 0.75$ min

81182.subject: Chemistry
81182.text: Which complex compound is most stable?
81182.sol:
Chelating ligands in general form more stable complexes than their monodentate analogs. When a chelating ligand binds to a metal ion, it forms a ring structure with the metal ion at the center. This ring structure increases the stability of the complex because it restricts the movement of the metal ion and prevents it from interacting with other molecules or ions. In addition, the chelating ligand can donate multiple electron pairs to the metal ion, which increases the strength of the metal-ligand bond and further stabilizes the complex.

∴ The most stable complex is $\left[{CoCl}_{2}{\left(en\right)}_{2}\right]{NO}_{3}$

84481.subject: Zoology
84481.text: Which of the following is correct regarding AIDS causative agent HIV?
options: HIV is an enveloped virus containing one molecule of single-stranded RNA and one molecule of reverse transcriptase.
HIV is an enveloped virus that contains two identical molecules of single-stranded RNA and two molecules of reverse transcriptase.
HIV does not escape but attacks the acquired immune response.
84481.sol:
The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) causes AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) and interferes with the body's ability to fight infection. The HIV infects macrophages and TH cells and upon infection, it inactivates these cells and hence, suppresses the immune system.

The structure of the virus is such that it is enveloped with a viral envelope (consists of a bilipid layer and proteins) inside which two identical molecules of single-stranded RNA molecules and two molecules of reverse transcriptase are present. The reverse transcriptase enzyme generates viral DNA inside the host by using viral RNA as a template.

85026.subject: Zoology
options: Nociceptors respond to changes in pressure
Photoreceptors in the human eye are depolarised during darkness and become hyperpolarized in response to the light stimulus
Receptors do not produce graded potentials
85026.sol:
Mechanism of vision: In the dark photoreceptors release an inhibitory neurotransmitter that prevents the activation of ganglion cells by bipolar neurons. Light inhibits the photoreceptors from releasing the inhibitory transmitter. Without this inhibition, the bipolar neurons are able to stimulate the ganglion cells. The ganglion cells transmit action cortex analyses and compare the input with earlier stored experiences for understanding the input (image).
The photoreceptors contain many Na+ channels in their plasma membrane. In the dark these channels are open and Na+ ions enter inducing depolarization of photoreceptors and release of inhibitory neurotransmitters. In the light, the photopigments present in the receptors become converted from 11-cis-retinene to all –trans-retinene. The trans-retinene gets dissociated from opsin protein. This brings up the closing of Ca+2 channels and opens up of Na+ channels and the potential gradient is formed. The photoreceptors do not release the inhibitory neurotransmitter hence, the bipolar neurons release excitatory neurotransmitters stimulating ganglion cells.

93353.subject: Physics
93353.text: A nozzle throws a stream of gas against a wall with a velocity $\text{v}$ much larger than the thermal agitation of the molecules. After collision of the molecules with wall the magnitude of their velocity remains same. Also assume that the force exerted on the wall by the molecules is perpendicular to wall. (This is not strictly true for a rough wall.) Find the pressure exerted on the wall. $(\text{n} =$ number of molecules per unit volume, $m =$mass of a gas molecule$)$
93353.sol:
Since, the molecules rebound from the wall, the component of velocity perpendicular to wall is reversed,  while its velocity parallel to wall does not change. The change in velocity of molecules is parallel to normal N. The magnitude of charge is

                         $\left|\Delta \overset{\to}{\text{v}}\right| = 2 v ⁡ \text{cos} \theta$

The change in momentum of a molecule is

                         $\left|\Delta \overset{\to}{\text{p}}\right| = m ⁡ \left|\Delta \overset{\to}{\text{v}}\right|

                          $= 2 m ⁡ v ⁡ $\text{cos}$ \theta$

in the direction of normal N. Let n be the number of molecules per unit volume.The number of molecules arriving at an area A of the wall per unit time is the number in a slanted cylinder whose length is equal to the velocity v and whose cross-section is $Acos\theta$

       Number of molecules $= n$\left(Avcos\theta\right)$.

Each molecule suffers a change of momentum $2mvcos\theta$. Change of momentum of the stream of gas in a direction perpendicular to wall is equal to $\left(nAvcos\theta\right) \times \left(2mvcos \theta\right) = 2An{mv}^{2}{cos}^{2}\theta$.

Hence, force exerted by stream of gas on the wall.

                        $F ⁡ = 2\text{A}n{\text{mv}}^{2}{\text{cos}}^{2}\theta$

This is also the force exerted by gas molecules on the wall.

                        $\text{Pressure} = \dfrac{\text{Normal force}}{\text{Area}}$

                            $= \dfrac{F ⁡}{A ⁡}$

                            $= 2n ⁡ m ⁡ v{⁡}^{2}{\text{cos}}^{2}\theta$

93735.text: Two soap bubbles are combined isothermally to form a single bubble. In this process, the change in volume and surface area are respectively $V$ and $A$. If $p$ is the atmospheric pressure, and $S$ is the surface tension of the soap solution, the correct relation, among the following, is
93735.sol:
Let the radii of the two soap bubble be& $a$ and $b$, respectively, and radius of a single larger bubble be $c$.

As excess pressure for a soap bubble is $\dfrac{4S}{r}$ and external pressure is $p$,

${p}_{i} = p + \dfrac{4S}{r}$

So, ${p}_{a} = p + \dfrac{4S}{a}, {p}_{b} = p + \dfrac{4S}{b}$

and ${p}_{c} = p + \dfrac{4T}{c}$ ...(i)

and& ${V}_{a} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pia^{3}, {V}_{b} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pib^{3}$

and ${V}_{c} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pic^{3}$ ...(ii)

Now, as mass is conserved,

${μ}_{a} + {μ}_{b} = {μ}_{c}$

$i . e . , \dfrac{{p}_{a}{V}_{a}}{R{T}_{a}} + \dfrac{{p}_{b}{V}_{b}}{R{T}_{b}} = \dfrac{{p}_{c}{V}_{c}}{R{T}_{c}} \left(aspV = \muRT\right)$

As the temperature is constant,

$i . e . , {T}_{a} = {T}_{b} = {T}_{c}$

So, ${p}_{a}{V}_{a} + {p}_{b}{V}_{b} = {p}_{c}{V}_{c}$

This, in the light of eqns. (i) and (ii) becomes,

$\left(p + \dfrac{4S}{a}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pia^{3}\right) + \left($ p + $\dfrac{4S}{b}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pib^{3}\right) = \left(p + \dfrac{4S}{c}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pic^{3}\right)$

$i . e . , 4S \left($ a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}\right) = p $\left($ c^{3} - a^{3} - b^{3}\right)$ ...(iii)

Now,& $V = $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left($ a^{3} + b^{3} - c^{3}\right)$

and $A = $4\pi \left($ a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}\right)$

$∴ $\dfrac{SA}{\pi} = - \dfrac{3Vp}{4\pi}$

or $4SA + 3pV = 0$

93999.subject: Physics
93999.text: A radioactive material decays by simultaneous emission of two particles with half-lives $1620$ years and $810$ years respectively. The time in years after which one - fourth of material remains, is
93999.sol:
Since, from Rutherford - Soddy law, the number of atoms left after half-lives is given by

$N = {N}_{0}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n}$

Where, ${N}_{0}$ is the original number of atoms.

The number of half-lives, $n = \dfrac{timeofdecay}{effectivehalf - life}$

Relation between effective disintegration constant $\left(\lambda\right)$ and half life $\left(T\right)$

$\lambda = \dfrac{ln ⁡ 2}{T}$

$∴ {\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2} = \dfrac{ln ⁡ 2}{{T}_{1}} + \dfrac{ln ⁡ 2}{{T}_{2}}$

Effective half life,

$\dfrac{1}{T} = \dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{1620} + \dfrac{1}{810}$

$\dfrac{1}{T} = \dfrac{1 + 2}{1620} ⇒ T = 540$~years

$∴ n = \dfrac{T}{540}$

$∴ N = {N}_{0}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{t}{540}} ⇒ \dfrac{N}{{N}_{0}} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{t}{540}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{t}{540} = 2 ⇒ t = 2 \times 540 = 1080$& years

96925.text:
Select the correct statements.
(A)& From the region of elongation, some of the epidermal cells form root hairs.
(B)& Pneumatophores are seen in Rhizophora.
(C)& Adventitious roots are seen in the banyan tree.
(D)& Maize and sugarcane have prop roots.
96925.sol:
The zone of elongation region of a root lies behind the growing point. The cells of this region are newly formed cells which lose the power of division. They elongate rapidly. This increases the length of the root. The external cells possess the power of absorption of water and minerals salts from the soil. The root hair zone represents the zone of differentiation or maturation because different types of primary tissues differentiate or mature in this region. Some of the outer cells of this zone give rise to lateral tubular outgrowths called root hairs.
Maize and sugarcane have stilt roots. These are short but thick supporting roots which develop obliquely from the basal nodes of the stem.

101019.subject: Physics
101019.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
101019.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a light body and a heavy body have the same linear momentum, the light body will cover a greater distance in a given time interval.
Reason (R): For a given linear momentum, the velocity of a body is inversely proportional to its mass.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
101019.sol:
Linear momentum is given by $p = mv$, which implies $v = \dfrac{p}{m}$.

For a constant linear momentum $p$, the velocity $v$ is inversely proportional to the mass $m$ ($v \propto \dfrac{1}{m}$). Therefore, a light body (smaller mass) will have a greater velocity compared to a heavy body. This makes the Reason (R) correct.

The distance covered in a given time interval $t$ is $d = vt$. Since the light body has a greater velocity, it will cover a greater distance in the same time interval. This makes the Assertion (A) correct.

The Reason (R) provides the exact formulaic relationship that explains why the light body has a higher velocity and consequently covers more distance. Thus, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

101176.subject: Physics
101176.text: Two identical uniform solid spheres, each of mass $M$ and radius $R$, have their centres connected by a light rigid rod of length $2R$. The radius of gyration of this combined system about an axis passing through the centre of the rod and perpendicular to its length is:
101176.sol:
The axis of rotation passes through the centre of the rod of length $2R$. The distance from this axis to the centre of each sphere is $R$.

The moment of inertia of one solid sphere about its own diametric axis is $I_{cm} = \dfrac{2}{5} M R^2$.
Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of one sphere about the given axis of rotation is:
$I_{sphere} = I_{cm} + M d^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} M R^2 + M R^2 = \dfrac{7}{5} M R^2$

Since there are two identical spheres, the total moment of inertia of the system is:
$I_{system} = 2 \times \dfrac{7}{5} M R^2 = \dfrac{14}{5} M R^2$

The total mass of the system is $M_{total} = 2M$.
Let $K$ be the radius of gyration of the system. Then $I_{system} = M_{total} K^2$.
$\dfrac{14}{5} M R^2 = (2M) K^2$
$K^2 = \dfrac{7}{5} R^2$
$K = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{5}} R$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{5}} R$

101882.subject: Physics
101882.text: Three heat-conducting rods of identical length and uniform cross-sectional area are joined at a common point to form a Y-shaped junction. The thermal conductivities of the three rods are $K$, $2K$, and $3K$. The free ends of the rods with conductivities $K$, $2K$, and $3K$ are maintained at steady temperatures of $100^{\circ}\text{C}$, $40^{\circ}\text{C}$, and $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ respectively. Assuming no heat loss from the lateral surfaces, the steady-state temperature of the central junction is:
101882.sol:
Let the steady-state temperature of the central junction be $T_J$.

According to Kirchhoff's junction rule for heat (conservation of energy), the net rate of heat flow into the junction must be zero in steady state.
$\Sigma H = 0$
$H_1 + H_2 + H_3 = 0$

Using the formula for heat current $H = \dfrac{KA(T_{\text{end}} - T_J)}{L}$, we can write:
$\dfrac{K A (100 - T_J)}{L} + \dfrac{2K A (40 - T_J)}{L} + \dfrac{3K A (0 - T_J)}{L} = 0$

Since $A$ and $L$ are identical for all rods, we can divide the entire equation by $\dfrac{KA}{L}$:
$(100 - T_J) + 2(40 - T_J) + 3(0 - T_J) = 0$

Expanding the terms:
100 - $T_J$ + 80 - $2T_J$ - $3T_J$ = 0
180 - $6T_J$ = 0
$6T_J$ = 180
$T_J = 30^{\circ}\text{C}$

Answer: $30^{\circ}\text{C}$

102439.subject: Physics
102439.text: A car is travelling at a constant speed $v$ on a flat horizontal circular track of radius $R$. While the car is negotiating a turn to the left, a simple pendulum suspended from the roof of the car tilts away from its vertical position. What is the direction of the pendulum's tilt relative to the car, and its angle of inclination with the vertical?
options: To the left, and the angle of inclination is $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{v^2}{Rg}\right)$
To the right, and the angle of inclination is $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{v^2}{Rg}\right)$
To the right, and the angle of inclination is $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{v^2}{Rg}\right)$
To the right, and the angle of inclination is $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{Rg}{v^2}\right)$
102439.sol:
When the car takes a turn to the left, it undergoes a centripetal acceleration directed towards the center of the circular path (to the left).

In the non-inertial frame of the car, a centrifugal pseudo force acts on the pendulum bob in the direction opposite to the acceleration, which is radially outward (to the right). Thus, the pendulum tilts to the right.

The magnitude of the centrifugal force is $F_c = \dfrac{mv^2}{R}$, acting horizontally, while the gravitational force $mg$ acts vertically downwards.

At equilibrium, the angle $\theta$ of the pendulum with the vertical is determined by the ratio of these forces:
$\tan \theta = \dfrac{F_c}{mg} = \dfrac{mv^2 / R}{mg} = \dfrac{v^2}{Rg}$

Therefore, the angle of inclination is $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{v^2}{Rg}\right)$.

Answer: To the right, and the angle of inclination is $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{v^2}{Rg}\right)$

103705.subject: Physics
103705.text: A long straight solid cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carries a steady uniform current along its length. If the magnitude of the magnetic field at a radial distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from the axis of the conductor is $B_{0}$, what will be the magnitude of the magnetic field at a radial distance of $3R$ from the axis?
103705.sol:
For a solid cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carrying a steady current $I$, the magnetic field inside the conductor ($r < R$) is given by:
$B_{in} = \dfrac{\mu_{0} I r}{2\pi R^{2}}$

At $r = \dfrac{R}{2}$:
$B_{0} = \dfrac{\mu_{0} I \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)}{2\pi R^{2}} = \dfrac{\mu_{0} I}{4\pi R}$

From this, we get $\mu_{0} I = 4\pi R B_{0}$.

The magnetic field outside the conductor ($r > R$) is given by:
$B_{out} = \dfrac{\mu_{0} I}{2\pi r}$

At $r = 3R$:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_{0} I}{2\pi (3R)} = \dfrac{\mu_{0} I}{6\pi R}$

Substituting the value of $\mu_{0} I$:
$B = \dfrac{4\pi R B_{0}}{6\pi R} = \dfrac{2}{3} B_{0}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2B_{0}}{3}$

103919.subject: Physics
103919.text: Two distinct inductors store the exact same amount of magnetic energy. If the ratio of their inductances is $1:4$, what is the ratio of the currents flowing through them?
103919.sol:
Let the inductances be $L_1 and L_2$, and the currents be $i_1 and i_2$.

The magnetic energy stored in an inductor is given by $U = \dfrac{1}{2} L i^2$.

Since the energies are equal:
$U_1 = U_2$
$\dfrac{1}{2} L_1 i_1^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} L_2 i_2^2$

Rearranging for the ratio of currents:
$\left(\dfrac{i_1}{i_2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{L_2}{L_1}$

Given that $L_1 : L_2 = 1 : 4$, we have $\dfrac{L_2}{L_1} = \dfrac{4}{1}$.

$\left(\dfrac{i_1}{i_2}\right)^2 = 4$
$\dfrac{i_1}{i_2} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

Therefore, the ratio of the currents is $2:1$.

Answer: $2:1$

104614.sol:
When a ray of light travels from one medium to the second medium, it bends. If first medium is
rarer and second medium is denser, it bends towards the normal while if first medium is denser and second medium is rarer, it bends away from the normal. This bending is due to refractive index of second medium with respect to first.
The refractive index is related to the speed of light in the two media as below :
${ }_1 \mu_2=\frac{\text{ speed of light in first medium }}{\text{ speed of light in second medium }}$
or speed of light in second medium
$=\frac{\text{ speed of light in first medium }}{{ }_1 \mu_2}$
where ${ }_1 \mu_2$ is refractive index of second medium relative to the first medium.
Hence, we see that on passing through another medium speed of light changes.

(B) Sulphur(II) Violet colour with sodium nitroprusside

111898.sol:
In Lassaigne's test for organic compounds:

Nitrogen forms sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), which reacts with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give a Prussian blue colour of $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$.

Chlorine forms sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$), which reacts with $\text{AgNO}_3$ to give a white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$ that is soluble in ammonium hydroxide.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

114897.subject: Chemistry
114897.text: A first-order reaction has a half-life of $100 \text{ s}$. If the initial concentration of the reactant is $0.2 \text{ M}$, what will be the instantaneous rate of the reaction after $200 \text{ s}$?
114897.sol:
The rate constant $k$ for a first-order reaction is related to its half-life by:

$k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{100} = 6.93 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}^{-1}$

The time elapsed is $200 \text{ s}$, which corresponds to exactly two half-lives ($n = \dfrac{200}{100} = 2$).

The concentration of the reactant remaining after two half-lives is:

$[A]_t = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2^n} = \dfrac{0.2}{2^2} = \dfrac{0.2}{4} = 0.05 \text{ M}$

The instantaneous rate of the reaction at this time is given by the differential rate law:

$\text{Rate} = k[A]_t = (6.93 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}^{-1}) \times 0.05 \text{ M} = 3.465 \times 10^{-4} \text{ M s}^{-1}$

Using the initial concentration instead of the concentration at $200 \text{ s}$ leads to the incorrect initial rate of $1.386 \times 10^{-3} \text{ M s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $3.465 \times 10^{-4} \text{ M s}^{-1}$

117791.subject: Chemistry
117791.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The complex $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ is diamagnetic, while $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic.
Reason (R): Platinum is a 5d transition metal, and for 4d and 5d series metals, the crystal field splitting is very large, causing even weak field ligands like $\text{Cl}^-$ to force electron pairing.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
117791.sol:
In the complex $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, the central metal ion is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ which has a $3d^8$ electronic configuration. Since $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, it does not cause pairing of electrons. The complex undergoes $sp^3$ hybridization, forming a tetrahedral geometry with 2 unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

In the complex $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$, the central metal ion is $\text{Pt}^{2+}$ which has a $5d^8$ electronic configuration. For metals in the 4d and 5d transition series, the effective nuclear charge is higher and the d-orbitals are more spatially extended. This leads to a much larger crystal field splitting ($\Delta$) compared to the 3d series. The large $\Delta$ overcomes the pairing energy regardless of the ligand strength. Thus, even with a weak field ligand like $\text{Cl}^-$, electron pairing occurs. The complex undergoes $dsp^2$ hybridization, forming a square planar geometry with no unpaired electrons, making it diamagnetic.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

121684.subject: Botany
121684.text: What does the assumption in phylogenetic classification systems suggest about organisms in the same taxa?
options: They possess the same genetic makeup.
121684.sol: The earliest systems of classification used only gross superficial morphological characters such as habit, color, number and shape of leaves, etc. They were based mainly on vegetative characters or on the androecium structure (system given by Linnaeus). Such systems were artificial; they separated the closely related species since they were based on a few characteristics. Also, the artificial systems gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characteristics; this is not acceptable since we know that often the vegetative characters are more easily affected by the environment. At present <mark>phylogenetic classification systems based on evolutionary relationships between the various organisms are acceptable. This assumes that organisms belonging to the same taxa have a common ancestor.</mark> We now use information from many other sources too to help resolve difficulties in classification. These become more important when there is no supporting fossil evidence. Numerical Taxonomy which is now easily carried out using computers is based on all observable characteristics. Numbers and codes are assigned to all the characters and the data are then processed.

They are of paramount importance as primary producers of energy-rich compounds which form the basis of the food cycles of all aquatic animals. Many species of Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are among the 70 species of marine algae used as food. Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids (water holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae) and carrageen (red algae) which are used commercially. Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria are used to grow microbes and in preparations of ice-creams and jellies. Chlorella a unicellular alga rich in proteins is used as food supplement even by space travellers. The algae are divided into three main classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.

121797.subject: Botany
121797.text: What is produced within the capsule of the sporophyte in liverworts?
121797.sol: The liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid, e.g., Marchantia. The thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows on the stem-like structures. Asexual reproduction in liverworts takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialized structures called gemmae (sing. gemma). Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds, which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli. The gemmae become detached from the parent body and germinate to form new individuals. During sexual reproduction, male and female sex organs are produced either on the same or on different thalli. The sporophyte is differentiated into a foot, seta and capsule. <mark>After meiosis, spores are produced within the capsule. These spores germinate to form free-living gametophytes</mark>.

123876.subject: Botany
123876.text:
Read the following statements describing key cellular events during the cell cycle:

(I) DNA replication begins in the nucleus.
(II) Condensation of chromosomal material begins.
(III) The cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.
(IV) Proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

Starting immediately after cell division, what is the correct chronological sequence of these events?
123876.sol:
According to NCERT, the interphase is divided into three phases: $\text{G}_{1}$, S, and $\text{G}_{2}$, followed by the M phase.

Statement (III) describes the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase (Gap 1), which occurs immediately after cell division. The cell is metabolically active and grows but does not replicate its DNA.
Statement (I) describes the S phase (Synthesis), where DNA replication begins.
Statement (IV) describes the $\text{G}_{2}$ phase (Gap 2), where proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis.
Statement (II) describes prophase, which is the initiation of the M phase (Mitosis).

Therefore, the correct chronological sequence is $\text{G}_{1} \rightarrow \text{S} \rightarrow \text{G}_{2} \rightarrow \text{M}$, which corresponds to III $\rightarrow$ I $\rightarrow$ IV $\rightarrow$ II.

Answer: III $\rightarrow$ I $\rightarrow$ IV $\rightarrow$ II

125169.sol:
Statement A is correct: Sucrose is converted into one molecule of glucose and one molecule of fructose by the enzyme invertase. Both monosaccharides enter glycolysis, each yielding a net gain of 2 ATP molecules, resulting in a total net gain of 4 ATP molecules.

Statement B is correct: The conversion of one molecule of 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde (PGAL) to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (BPGA) produces one molecule of NADH + H$^+$.

Statement C is incorrect: The gross (total) production of ATP during glycolysis of one glucose molecule is 4 molecules, while the net gain is 2 molecules.

Statement D is incorrect: Fructose is phosphorylated by the enzyme hexokinase to enter the glycolytic pathway, a step that utilises ATP.

Therefore, exactly two statements (A and B) are correct.

Answer: Two

126306.subject: Botany
126306.text: Identify which of the following fruits are false fruits?
126306.sol: Apple and strawberry are false fruits. In apple, the fruit is pome which is a false or accessory simple succulent fruit that develops from an inferior compound ovary. The outer fleshy part of apple is thalamus. Strawberry is an aggregate accessory fruit. The fleshy part of the fruit is derived from the receptacle that holds the ovary. In mango and coconut, the fruit is known as drupe. They develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one seeded. In mango the pericarp is well differentiated into an outer thin epicarp, a middle fleshy edible mesocarp and an inner stony hard endocarp. In coconut which is also a drupe, the mesocarp is fibrous.

126397.subject: Botany
126397.text: Which of the following flowers only once in its life-time?

126721.subject: Botany
126721.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Palmitic acid and arachidonic acid are classified as lipids, whereas glutamic acid is classified as an amino acid.
Reason (R): Fatty acids have a carboxyl group attached to an R group (containing 1 to 19 carbons), whereas amino acids contain an amino group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen atom, and a variable R group attached to the same $\alpha$-carbon.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
126721.sol:
Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Despite all three molecules containing a carboxyl (acidic) group, they belong to different biochemical categories based on their core structures. According to NCERT, fatty acids (which are lipids) consist of a carboxyl group attached to a hydrocarbon R group that can have 1 to 19 carbons. Palmitic acid (16 carbons) and arachidonic acid (20 carbons) fit this structural definition.

On the other hand, amino acids are defined by having an amino group and an acidic (carboxyl) group as substituents on the same $\alpha$-carbon. Glutamic acid fits this structural definition and is thus classified as an amino acid.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

126791.subject: Botany
126791.text: Select the incorrect match regarding the biomolecule, its biological function, and the type of bond linking its monomers:
options: GLUT-4 $\rightarrow$ Enables glucose transport into cells $\rightarrow$ Glycosidic bond
Collagen $\rightarrow$ Intercellular ground substance $\rightarrow$ Peptide bond
Antibody $\rightarrow$ Fights infectious agents $\rightarrow$ Peptide bond
126791.sol:
According to NCERT, GLUT-4, collagen, trypsin, and antibodies are all proteins. Proteins are polypeptides, which are linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.



GLUT-4 is a protein that enables glucose transport into cells. Since it is a protein, its monomers (amino acids) are linked by peptide bonds, not glycosidic bonds. Glycosidic bonds are characteristic of polysaccharides (carbohydrates).



Therefore, the match for GLUT-4 is incorrect.



Answer: GLUT-4 $\rightarrow$ Enables glucose transport into cells $\rightarrow$ Glycosidic bond

127148.subject: Botany
127148.text: How many species of plants have been recorded from India?
127148.sol: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world. Nearly 45,000 species of plants and twice as many of animals have been recorded from India. How many living species are actually there waiting to be discovered and named? If we accept May’s global estimates, only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far. Applying this proportion to India’s diversity figures, we estimate that there are probably more than 1,00,000 plant species and more than 3,00,000 animal species yet to be discovered and described
127148.meta: How many species of plants have been recorded from India?

127187.subject: Botany
127187.text: How fast are species going extinct in the current episode of extinction compared to previous episodes?
127187.sol: During the long period (> 3 billion years) since the origin and diversification of life on earth there were five episodes of mass extinction of species. How is the ‘Sixth Extinction’ presently in progress different from the previous episodes? The difference is in the rates; the current species extinction rates are estimated to be 100 to 1,000 times faster than in the pre-human times and our activities are responsible for the faster rates. Ecologists warn that if the present trends continue, nearly half of all the species on earth might be wiped out within the next 100 years.
127187.meta: How fast are species going extinct in the current episode of extinction compared to previous episodes?

127204.subject: Botany
127204.text: What is the impact of invasive weed species like carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana and water hyacinth (EicchorniA) on our native species?
127204.sol: When alien species are introduced unintentionally or deliberately for whatever purpose, some of them turn invasive, and cause decline or extinction of indigenous species. The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in east Africa led eventually to the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of more than 200 species of cichlid fish in the lake. You must be familiar with the environmental damage caused and threat posed to our native species by invasive weed species like carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana and water hyacinth (Eicchornia). The recent illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture purposes is posing a threat to the indigenous catfishes in our rivers

127611.subject: Botany
127611.text: What is the standing crop in a food chain?
options: The mass of living material at a particular time in a specific area
The amount of energy at a particular time in a specific area
The number of organisms at a particular time in a specific area
The biomass of a species in a specific area
127611.sol: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called as the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. The biomass of a species is expressed in terms of fresh or dry weight. Measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate. Why?The number of trophic levels in the grazing food chain is restricted as the transfer of energy follows 10 per cent law – only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level. In nature, it is possible to have so many levels – producer, herbivore, primary carnivore, secondary carnivore in the grazing food chain

127739.subject: Botany
127739.text:
ConceptDescription
A. Trophic Level1. A functional level representing feeding position
B. Pyramid of Energy2. Shows number of organisms at each trophic level
C. Pyramid of Biomass3. Can be inverted in aquatic ecosystems
D. Pyramid of Numbers4. Always upright due to energy loss as heat
127739.sol:
Trophic Level (A) represents a functional level in an ecosystem (1), such as producers, herbivores, or carnivores.
Pyramid of Numbers (D) depicts the number of organisms at each trophic level (2).
Pyramid of Biomass (C) can be inverted in aquatic ecosystems (3), where the biomass of fish can exceed that of phytoplankton.
Pyramid of Energy (B) is always upright (4) because energy decreases with each trophic level due to heat loss.

127835.subject: Botany
127835.text: What is the Greek word for ecology?
127835.sol: The term ecology was coined by combining two Greek words, oikos (meaning 'house' or 'dwelling place') and logos (meaning 'the study of') to denote such relationships between the organisms and their environment. Thus, literally, ecology is the study of organisms 'at home'.
